title: Interaction Fragments — rough proto + dev notes
content:
Quick brain dump / scratchpad for 'Interaction Fragments' feature (developer-facing).

Problem space (user-visible):
- Developers building assistants frequently recreate small deterministic interactions (confirmations, short guided flows, entity-collection micro-flows) across endpoints.
- Repetition increases prompt surface area, token cost, and makes rollouts/hotfixing brittle.
- Need quick, composable building blocks that can be edited centrally, reused across routes, and optionally executed at lower fidelity/cost.

Hypothesis / value prop:
- Provide a fragments library (name + small instruction + optional schema + metadata) that teams can reference from prompts or call via SDK.
- Centralized fragment editing enables bug fixes and UX tweaks without touching product code; reduces duplicate prompt text and token usage.
- Fragment execution can be served by lightweight local renderer (short templates) or by full LLM call depending on fidelity policy -> cost savings.

Core primitives (rough):
1) Fragment (immutable versioned object): id, name, role (system/user/instruction), template (templating language), schema (json-ish), examples, tags.
2) Fragment Reference: in prompt text or SDK you can insert {{fragment:confirm-email-v1}} or call fragments.get("confirm-email", {context})
3) Execution policy: inline/local-template | hosted-llm | hosted-llm-with-fallback. Configurable per-fragment/per-route.
4) Dev console + preview: author + test harness (runs fragment against sample context, shows token delta, latency estimate).

UX sketches (console):
- Fragments list: name, last-modified, version, token-est (avg), hit-rate.
- Fragment editor: WYSIWYG-ish template editor with sample variables panel and quick-run button.
- Route binding: in Redwood Console you can map a route/prompt template to a fragment set and choose policy overrides.

SDK / API (proto):
- POST /v1/fragments -> create (private team fragment)
- GET /v1/fragments/:id -> retrieve
- POST /v1/fragments/:id/run -> run with context -> returns either rendered string or LLM output depending on policy
- client.fragments.insertIntoPrompt(promptTemplate, {name:"confirm-email", vars}) -> returns substituted prompt

Developer stories (rough):
- As a product engineer, I want to author a "confirm-email" fragment once and reuse it across 6 assistant skills so I can update copy in one place.
- As a platform engineer, I want to route low-risk fragments to a templating runtime to cut token usage by ~30%.
- As an SRE, I want per-fragment telemetry (avg tokens, p95 latency, error-rate) to detect regressions when a fragment is edited.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Create / update / list fragments via API + Console editor (team-scoped) -> basic versioning (v1,v2)
- Ability to reference fragment from a hosted prompt template and see rendered result in the prompt preview
- Execution policies: local-template (no LLM call) and hosted-llm (LLM call); clear token accounting for both
- Console shows token delta when fragment is inserted (expected token savings vs inline)
- Basic telemetry: tokens per run, latency p50/p95, error count

Metrics to measure success:
- Adoption: # of fragments created per org in first 60 days
- Reuse ratio: number of prompt templates referencing fragments / total templates
- Token savings: aggregate tokens saved (estimated) attributable to fragments
- Stability: fragment-related incidents (bugs/regressions) per month
- Developer satisfaction (qualitative) via survey after 30 days

Risks & open questions:
- Security: fragments may contain sensitive instructions. Need scoping (team-private vs org-shared) and KMS/Audit logs?
- Versioning model: optimistic about simple vN labels, but need immutable snapshots and an easy rollback UX.
- Template language: stick to safe subset (mustache-like) or allow mini-programs? Simpler is safer initially.
- Testing: how to prevent fragment edits from silently changing behavior in production? Consider canary flagging or staged rollouts.
- Migration: how to detect duplicated inline copy across existing prompts and recommend migration candidates?

Implementation notes / infra sketch:
- Fragments stored as JSON + versioning in metadata DB (owner, team, tags)
- Lightweight renderer service (stateless) for local-template policy; sandbox variables and basic guards
- Metrics emitted via existing tracing pipeline (route + fragment id tags)
- Console: reuse prompt preview component; add fragment chooser overlay

Small prototype plan (2 sprints):
Sprint 1 (proto):
- Basic fragment model + API create/get/list
- Console fragment editor (minimal) and ability to insert into prompt preview (client-side substitution)
- Local-template renderer (serverless function) + token-estimator
- Instrument token accounting

Sprint 2 (proto->beta):
- Add run endpoint with hosted-llm execution
- Add versioning UI and simple rollback
- Add telemetry dashboard for fragments
- Add migration helper script (scan templates, fuzzy match candidates)

Quick CLI/SDK examples (notes):
- JS: const frag = await client.fragments.create({name:'confirm-email', template:'Please confirm {{email}}.'})
- Insert: const prompt = await client.fragments.insertIntoPrompt('Hi, {{fragment:confirm-email}}', {email:'a@b.com'})

To-dos / immediate next steps:
- Pair with Mika to scope rendered template safety (XSS-like vector in downstream clients)
- Spike: run a scan across existing prompt templates to find top 50 duplicated snippets (JIRA:INFR-245)
- Mock console wires and get quick product feedback (reach out to Rhea/Kate)
- Draft a one-pager for internal sync: why fragments, expected runway + rough cost savings estimate

Notes to self:
- Keep MVP conservative: stick to template substitution + optional LLM run. No scripting v1.
- Focus telemetry early — visibility makes adoption safer for platform teams.

Slack references I mentioned while thinking: #prod-tooling, #fragments-proto, thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C12345/p1672345678901234

End of jot. This is messy — intended. Will refine into a PRD if traction.
